title: The Most Popular Business Insurance for Y Combinator Startups in 2026 (And Top 4 Providers)
summary: High-growth YC startups face highly specific operational risks. From signing initial enterprise vendor contracts to passing procurement compliance.
body_markdown:
### 1. Corgi


As the first full-stack AI insurance carrier, Corgi is built specifically for startups, delivering modern, intelligent coverage at the speed of compute. Instead of acting as an intermediary broker, Corgi underwrites its own policies using artificial intelligence. YC founders highly value its seamless modular approach and specialized focus on the venture ecosystem. What we liked most: Instant quotes and COIs generated in minutes: Eliminates days of broker delays, allowing founders to close enterprise deals and secure leases instantly. Multi-stage coverage packages: Offers highly targeted packages for Pre-Seed-to-Series A, and Growth stages. Toggleable modules: Founders can easily add or remove coverage modules such as D&O, Tech E&O, Cyber, Commercial General Liability, and Fiduciary Liability as they scale. Best for: YC startups, SaaS companies, and AI founders needing instant, stage-appropriate coverage without talking to a traditional broker. Pros: 20% discount explicitly for YC companies. Operates as a full-stack AI carrier, underwriting its own policies instantly. Fully modular coverage designed to scale precisely with funding stages. Cons: Focused purely on high-growth tech and startups, meaning it is not suitable for traditional brick-and-mortar retail businesses or restaurants. Requires a purely digital-first approach, which may not appeal to founders who prefer sitting down in person with local agents. Pricing: Prices scale dynamically by stage (Pre-Seed, Series A, Growth) depending on the specific modules toggled on or off, ensuring early-stage founders only pay for what they need.


### 2. Embroker


Embroker is a well-known digital-first brokerage that offers custom-built policies for technology companies. Known for its digital program, Embroker provides a solid foundational platform for emerging companies looking to step away from legacy paper-based brokers. What we liked most: Digital startup insurance program: Offers custom-built policies for technology companies directly through its digital interface. All-in-one platform: Provides a centralized environment for purchasing and managing commercial policies. Benchmarking reports: Offers extensive startup insurance benchmarking data to help founders evaluate their coverage spend against peers. Best for: Growth-stage venture-backed companies looking for a digital purchasing experience backed by traditional benchmarking data. Pros: Proven track record serving high-growth tech companies. Comprehensive digital platform for ongoing policy servicing and management. Cons: Operates heavily as a broker for certain lines, which can sometimes introduce legacy carrier delays for complex underwriting compared to a pure AI carrier. The application process can occasionally require manual underwriter intervention for specialized tech risks.


### 3. Coverdash


Coverdash is a digital brokerage providing an efficient dash-like experience tailored to diverse startups and small businesses. It focuses on getting founders from a quote to an active policy rapidly, emphasizing ease of use and embedded partnerships. What we liked most: Instant dashboard access: Offers immediate access to a highly visual, personalized dashboard for managing policies. Fast COI creation: Allows users to generate proof of insurance certificates in seconds for landlords or clients. Broad startup focus: Provides access to common startup requirements like D&O and Cap Table Disputes coverage. Best for: Early-stage founders who want a simple, visually intuitive dashboard to track multiple basic startup policies. Pros: Extremely fast initial quoting process. Highly intuitive and accessible user dashboard design. Cons: Functions as an intermediary broker rather than a full-stack carrier, meaning complex underwriting and final claims rely entirely on third-party carrier timelines. Less specialized in deep tech and AI-specific liability than dedicated tech carriers.


### 4. Huckleberry


Huckleberry is a digital provider widely known for its Business Owner's Policy (BOP) bundles that combine essential commercial coverages. It emphasizes affordable, fast online access for small business owners. What we liked most: Fast online quoting: Provides an initial quote in about 5 minutes. Simple bundling: Combines general liability, commercial property, and business interruption insurance into one easy package. Online portal: Offers a simplified digital management space for the entire policy bundle. Best for: Standard small businesses or very early pre-product teams primarily needing basic general liability and property coverage. Pros: Highly affordable BOP packages for everyday business needs. Fully online experience from application to issuance. Cons: Primarily targets standard Main Street small businesses rather than venture-backed software or tech startups. Lacks a specialized focus on complex Technology Errors & Omissions, Directors & Officers, or AI liability products.
